Figure 1:Overview of Omni-InteractScope.Top:Representative interactions connect user requests or general assistance needs with events in audiovisual streams and the content and timing of the required responses. The examples span event-timed tool invocation, a gesture reminder conditioned on an image and text request, and hearing
assistance under a general instruction without an event-specific query.Bottom:Distributions of task types, scene categories, and stream durations across the benchmark’s 1,479 interactions. Clips reused across multiple interactions are counted once for each interaction in which they appear.

Figure 2:Representative interactions across the eight task groups of Omni-InteractScope.Each panel links a user request (Q), timestamped stream observations, and reference responses (A) to illustrate what intervention is required and when. The colored diamonds mark reference response times. T6 includes an image and text request, while T7 and the T8-C guidance example show how a single request can require successive responses as the stream unfolds.

Figure 4:An annotated cumulative-state interaction (T4).Three source frames show successive dish preparations. The request and reference
response are reproduced from the annotation. Count labels identify the illustrated
preparations, not model predictions. The evaluator derives[46,50][46,50]seconds
from the 48-second point target. The frame strip provides selected evidence;
the model observes the causal stream rather than this summary.

Figure 6:Step coverage and complete guidance on 20 three-step episodes.(a) Matched targets at each step position, with a denominator of 20 per cell.
(b) Observed complete counts, permutation expectations, and central 95%
reference intervals. Each permutation preserves the marginal counts in (a).
The reference does not model episode difficulty or identify a memory mechanism.

Figure 7:Acting early and giving the wrong reminder.(a) Gemini-3.5-Flash calls a tool at query arrival, before the scored window,
and repeats it at 29.00 s. The reference tool isimage_search; timing
already determines failure. (b) The still-lit M button is outlined in the source
frame. All five in-window Gemini-3.1-Pro responses recommend exit instead of
waiting. Two are quoted in full; other unmatched outputs are not thereby
classified as invalid assistance. Neither case establishes an internal cause.

Figure 8:C# diagnosis across three editing states.Source-frame crops accompany recorded replies at the indicated times. The request
and replies are translated from Chinese;[...]marks omissions.
The original target is a reminder to run tests at 60.50 s, against which the stored
outcome is premature. The displayed diagnoses illustrate agreement with the
screen, not additional scored targets.

Figure 9:Following a DaVinci Resolve import workflow.Original frames appear on the left. Panels (a,c) show source crops with matching
asset labels; (b) is a redrawn English reference dialog.††footnotemark:The diamond marks the annotated second-method point (189.87 s), with its±2\pm 2-second window shaded. Circles mark the request and first replies.

Figure 10:Two covered steps with an incomplete final instruction.Each column pairs a source state with the full reference and a recorded
Gemini-3.1-Pro response. The first two columns show stored matches; the third
shows one of four incorrect final-target candidates. The shelf location and
closing action distinguish the reference from the prediction. Frame timestamps
identify sampled evidence, while output timestamps identify model emissions.
An incorrect 21-second attempt does not prevent the later 22-second match under
ordered assignment.
